page: Microsoft Azure D8pls_v5 is an arm64-based virtual machine powered by Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 hardware operating at 3.0 GHz. Built upon Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per core, along with 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The server does not bundle local storage, requiring external premium network storage, and contains no hardware GPUs or included public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reflect mid-tier throughput across multi-core execution alongside weaker single-core compute. The system attained a multi-core stress-ng metric of 14505.83 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 6048.0, whereas Geekbench single-core registered in the bottom quartile at 1092.0. Memory bandwidth reached 94.59 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 48.87 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific tests reveal standard throughput in web serving (10.24 GB/sec), software compilation via Clang (9346.0), and Redis SET operations (11.2 million operations/sec), though text processing and single-threaded decompression show lower baseline efficiency.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the D8pls_v5 operates with reduced memory density relative to standard general-purpose profiles. This hardware setup offers predictable execution across all 8 dedicated cores without hyperthreading contention. It is suited for scale-out web serving, lightweight caching layers, CI/CD code compilation, and distributed microservices that do not rely on local NVMe disks or extensive RAM allocations.
description: Microsoft Azure D8pls_v5 is an ARM-based instance configured with 8 dedicated Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 physical cores running at 3.0 GHz and 16.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU). Based on Microsoft Hyper-V, it operates without simultaneous multithreading and includes 32 MB of L3 cache, but includes no local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing demonstrates solid mid-tier parallel compute, reaching 14505.83 in stress-ng multi-core and 11.2 million ops/sec in Redis SET operations, while single-thread results such as a 1092.0 Geekbench single-core score position it in the lower tiers. The 1:2 memory ratio provides cost-efficient, dedicated CPU capacity suitable for containerized microservices, build nodes, and web serving.
